01-evidence: Every experimental run separates into three operational stages—preparation, transformation, and measurement—logged as discrete detector clicks across triggered clock windows.

Finite sample counts fluctuate binomially with standard error scaling as \(1/\sqrt{N}\), whereas unbalanced detector efficiencies \(\eta_A \neq \eta_B\) introduce systematic postselection bias that more trials never erase.
Swapping physical detectors between output ports cancels asymmetric detection efficiencies via the geometric-mean estimator and exposes hidden apparatus assumptions.
02-energy: Discrete atomic spectral lines, the Franck–Hertz collision steps, and the photoelectric threshold \(K_{\max} = hf - \phi\) establish that energy exchange with matter and light occurs in quantized packets \(\Delta E = hf\).
Stopping-potential measurements show that maximum photoelectron kinetic energy depends linearly on optical frequency \(f\) with universal slope \(h/e\), independent of classical beam intensity.
Photodiode dark currents, reverse leakage, and collector-emitter contact potential differences must be calibrated before extracting Planck’s constant from threshold curves.
03-matter-waves: Electrons, neutrons, atoms, and molecules accumulate double-slit interference fringes with de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\) even when particles traverse the apparatus one at a time.
Each detection event is localized at a single pixel, while the probability density \(P(x) = |\psi_1(x) + \psi_2(x)|^2\) governs the long-run spatial envelope and fringe visibility \(\mathcal{V}\).
Transverse source size, velocity dispersion, mechanical vibration, and residual gas scattering reduce fringe contrast without turning individual clicks into smeared waves.
04-stern-gerlach: An inhomogeneous magnetic field splits a spin-\(\frac{1}{2}\) beam into exactly two discrete spatial components along the chosen gradient axis rather than a continuous classical band.

Projecting sequentially along axes separated by angle \(\theta\) transmits fraction \(\cos^2(\theta/2)\), and inserting an intermediate \(\hat{x}\) analyzer erases prior \(\hat{z}\) memory so \(|+z\rangle \to |+x\rangle \to |-z\rangle\) occurs with nonzero probability.
Blocking vs. recombining internal Stern–Gerlach paths distinguishes irreversible projective filtering from coherent unitary spin rotation.
05-polarization: Malus’s law \(I(\theta) = I_0 \cos^2\theta\) follows from projecting a linear polarization state \(|\theta\rangle = \cos\theta|H\rangle + \sin\theta|V\rangle\) onto the analyzer axis.

Inserting a diagonal polarizer at \(45^\circ\) between crossed \(H\) and \(V\) filters restores transmission from \(0\) to \(\frac{1}{4}\) because projection prepares a new coherent superposition rather than filtering pre-existing tags.
Real polarizers have finite extinction ratios, surface reflections, and retardance tolerances that set a nonzero floor on crossed-filter leakage.
06-photon-counting: Classical coherent or thermal light beams split at a beam splitter always satisfy the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality \(g^{(2)}(0) \ge 1\), whereas a true single-photon Fock state \(|1\rangle\) exhibits antibunching \(g^{(2)}(0) = 0\).

Heralded spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) suppresses accidental multi-pair coincidences \(g^{(2)}_h(0) \ll 1\) only in the low-pump-power regime where pair probability per window \(\mu \ll 1\).
Unheralded attenuated laser pulses remain Poissonian mixtures of vacuum, single, and multi-photon states regardless of how dim the filter is.
07-interferometer: In a balanced Mach–Zehnder interferometer, two 50:50 beam splitters that each act randomly in isolation combine via relative phase \(\phi\) to produce deterministic routing \(P_+ = \cos^2(\phi/2)\) at \(\phi = 0\) or \(\pi\).
Blocking either arm destroys the cross term \(\cos\phi\) and drops the output probability at each port from \(1\) (or \(0\)) to \(\frac{1}{4}\).
Wavefront mismatch, polarization drift between arms, and optical path fluctuations faster than the integration window degrade measured fringe visibility \(\mathcal{V}\).
08-recoiling-slit: In Einstein’s recoiling-slit thought experiment, measuring the slit’s transverse momentum kick \(\delta p_y\) to identify which path the particle took entangles the particle with the slit state \(|\phi_1\rangle, |\phi_2\rangle\).

Heisenberg’s position–momentum uncertainty \(\Delta y\,\Delta p_y \ge \hbar/2\) ensures that localizing the slit well enough to resolve a fringe spacing \(\Lambda\) makes the momentum kicks overlap, and vice versa.

The quantitative duality relation \(\mathcal{D}^2 + \mathcal{V}^2 \le 1\) bounds path distinguishability \(\mathcal{D}\) and interference visibility \(\mathcal{V} = |\langle\phi_1|\phi_2\rangle|\) continuously across all coupling strengths.
09-delayed-choice: Wheeler’s delayed-choice experiment inserts or removes the final beam splitter \(\mathrm{BS}_2\) by a fast electro-optic switch after the photon has already entered the interferometer.

When \(\mathrm{BS}_2\) is absent, detectors register equal path probabilities \(P = \frac{1}{2}\); when \(\mathrm{BS}_2\) is present, they register phase-dependent fringes \(\cos^2(\phi/2)\)—all computed forward in time from the unitary state evolution.
No retrocausal signal is sent into the past: the photon was never required to commit to a classical ‘particle-only’ or ‘wave-only’ biography at the first beam splitter.
10-quantum-eraser: When path-System entanglement marks which arm a particle took, the unconditional marginal signal distribution is a flat sum of two complementary fringe patterns \(\cos^2(\phi/2)\) and \(\sin^2(\phi/2)\) that add to \(1\).

Measuring the marker in the erased diagonal basis \(|\pm\rangle\) and sorting signal detections by coincidence outcome recovers full-visibility fringes (shifted by \(\pi\) between \(|+\rangle\) and \(|-\rangle\)).
Because the total marginal signal remains completely flat without classical coincidence sorting, quantum erasure never transmits faster-than-light messages.
11-interaction-free: In the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb tester, an absorbing object placed inside one arm of a tuned Mach–Zehnder interferometer breaks destructive interference at the dark port.
With a single 50:50 interferometer, \(25\%\) of trials click at the dark port without absorbing the photon, yielding a maximum efficiency of \(\eta = \frac{1}{3}\) per intact bomb.

Concatenating \(N\) weak reflective cycles of rotation angle \(\theta = \pi/(2N)\) via the quantum Zeno effect drives the absorption probability toward \(0\) and interaction-free efficiency toward \(1\).
12-tunnelling: Inside a classically forbidden rectangular barrier of height \(V_0 > E\) and width \(a\), the wavefunction decays evanescently with attenuation constant \(\kappa = \sqrt{2m(V_0 - E)}/\hbar\) rather than vanishing abruptly.

Boundary continuity at both interfaces yields non-zero transmission \(T \approx T_0 e^{-2\kappa a}\), whose exponential sensitivity to \(a\) and \(\sqrt{m(V_0-E)}\) powers scanning tunnelling microscopy and alpha decay.
Energy conservation holds strictly: a transmitted particle emerges on the far side with its full initial total energy \(E\), never with negative kinetic energy.
13-rabi: A near-resonant coherent drive couples states \(|0\rangle\) and \(|1\rangle\) with Rabi frequency \(\Omega\) and detuning \(\Delta\), rotating the state vector on the Bloch sphere at generalized rate \(\Omega_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sqrt{\Omega^2 + \Delta^2}\).

On resonance (\(\Delta = 0\)), a \(\pi/2\) pulse prepares an equal superposition and a \(\pi\) pulse inverts population completely, while nonzero detuning caps maximum inversion at \(\Omega^2/(\Omega^2+\Delta^2)\).
Finite relaxation \(T_1\), dephasing \(T_2\), and spatial drive inhomogeneities damp Rabi oscillations toward a mixed steady state at long pulse durations.
14-ramsey: Ramsey interferometry separates two \(\pi/2\) pulses by a free-precession interval \(\tau\), converting detuning \(\Delta\) into phase accumulation \(\phi = \Delta\tau\) and fringe oscillations \(\cos(\Delta\tau)\).
Inhomogeneous quasi-static frequency offsets across an ensemble cause free-induction fringes to decay on timescale \(T_2^*\), even when individual spins remain coherent.
Inserting a refocusing \(\pi\) Hahn spin-echo pulse at \(\tau/2\) reverses static phase dispersion and restores coherence up to the irreversible homogeneous decay time \(T_2\).
15-tomography: A single qubit’s density matrix \(\rho = \frac{1}{2}(I + r_x X + r_y Y + r_z Z)\) requires measurements along at least three linearly independent axes (\(X, Y, Z\)) because no single basis reveals both populations and phase coherences.
Direct linear inversion of noisy finite-sample frequencies \((\hat{r}_x, \hat{r}_y, \hat{r}_z)\) can yield unphysical vectors with \(\|\hat{\mathbf{r}}\| > 1\) and negative eigenvalues.
Constrained maximum-likelihood or least-squares estimation projects the reconstructed operator back onto the physical Bloch ball \(\|\mathbf{r}\| \le 1\) with bootstrap uncertainty regions.
16-two-photon: When two indistinguishable photons arrive simultaneously at opposite ports of a balanced 50:50 beam splitter, the reflection–reflection and transmission–transmission coincidence amplitudes interfere with opposite signs (\(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 0\)).
Scanning the arrival delay \(\Delta\tau\) traces out the Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) coincidence dip, where visibility exceeding \(50\%\) certifies nonclassical two-photon interference.

Polarization-entangled Bell pairs produce phase-sensitive two-photon fringes \(\cos^2(\alpha - \beta)\) across arbitrary analyzer settings while keeping each individual photon’s marginal statistics completely unpolarized.
17-epr-bell: Any local hidden-variable model that assigns pre-existing outcome rules \(A(a,\lambda), B(b,\lambda) \in \{\pm 1\}\) satisfies the Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) bound \(|S| \le 2\).

A singlet Bell state measured at relative analyzer angles of \(45^\circ\) achieves correlation \(E(a,b) = -\cos(a-b)\) and violates the CHSH inequality up to Tsirelson’s bound \(|S| = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828\).
Loophole-free Bell tests close the locality, detection-efficiency (\(\eta > 82.8\%\) for symmetric CHSH), and setting-independence loopholes simultaneously while respecting relativistic no-signaling.
18-ghz-contextuality: For the three-qubit Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state \(|\mathrm{GHZ}\rangle = (|000\rangle + |111\rangle)/\sqrt{2}\), multiplying the three commuting stabilizers \(X_1Y_2Y_3, Y_1X_2Y_3, Y_1Y_2X_3\) against \(X_1X_2X_3\) yields an algebraic sign contradiction (\(+1 = -1\)) for any noncontextual value assignment.
The Peres–Mermin magic square demonstrates state-independent contextuality on two qubits using nine observables arranged in six commuting rows and columns.
Experimental tests translate ideal deterministic paradoxes into noise-tolerant noncontextuality inequalities that account for finite gate fidelities and imperfect compatibility.
19-teleportation: Quantum teleportation transfers an unknown state \(|\psi\rangle\) using a shared Bell pair and two classical bits from Alice’s Bell-basis measurement so Bob can apply the matching Pauli correction \(X^{b_2}Z^{b_1}\).
Without Alice’s two classical bits, Bob’s local density matrix is the maximally mixed state \(I/2\) regardless of \(|\psi\rangle\), preserving relativistic causality.
Entanglement swapping teleports an entangled share itself, projecting two independent pairs \(AB\) and \(CD\) into an entangled pair \(AD\) conditioned on the middle Bell-state outcome.
20-schrodinger-cat: Unitary Schrödinger evolution maps a microscopic superposition coupled to a pointer into an entangled state \(\alpha|0\rangle|D_0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle|D_1\rangle\) rather than selecting a single macroscopic branch on its own.

Environmental scattering rapidly damps the off-diagonal coherence factor \(\gamma(t) = \langle E_1(t)|E_0(t)\rangle = e^{-\Gamma t}\), turning the reduced system–pointer state into a diagonal mixture in the pointer basis.
Decoherence explains why macroscopic interference cannot be observed locally and why the pointer basis is stable, while leaving the single-outcome measurement problem distinct.
21-wigners-friend: In Wigner’s friend scenario, an internal observer \(F\) describes her measurement by a projective state collapse, whereas an external superobserver \(W\) describes the isolated laboratory unitarily as an entangled state \(|\Phi\rangle_{SF}\).
As long as \(W\) does not perform coherent interference measurements that overwrite \(F\)’s memory register, both descriptions predict identical marginal probabilities for \(F\)’s recorded outcomes.
Testing \(|\Phi\rangle_{SF}\) in a coherent superobserver basis requires reversing the entire laboratory unitary—an operation that erases \(F\)’s classical record.
22-extended-friends: Brukner’s and Frauchiger–Renner’s extended Wigner’s friend scenarios couple two entangled laboratories so four observables \(A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2\) cannot share a single joint probability distribution \(P(A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2)\).

No-go theorems prove that four assumptions—universal unitary validity (Q), observer-independent single outcomes (A), local setting independence (L), and consistency across agents (C)—cannot all hold simultaneously.
Laboratory demonstrations using single-photon or qubit ‘friends’ test two-qubit unitary interference and Bell violations, not conscious macroscopic observers.
23-sensing: A Ramsey quantum sensor encodes an external magnetic field or clock frequency shift into a phase \(\phi = \gamma B\tau\), achieving maximum slope at the quadrature bias point \(\phi_0 = \pi/2\).

For \(N\) uncorrelated probes, quantum projection noise limits phase uncertainty to the Standard Quantum Limit \(\delta\phi_{\mathrm{SQL}} = 1/\sqrt{N}\), whereas \(N\)-partite GHZ or spin-squeezed states reach the Heisenberg scaling \(1/N\) in the absence of decoherence.
Under realistic dephasing at rate \(\gamma\), an \(N\)-qubit GHZ state decoheres \(N\) times faster than a single spin, requiring optimal interrogation times \(\tau \sim 1/(2\gamma)\).
24-investigation: Auditing an experimental quantum claim requires verifying every step from raw timestamped coincidence tables to background subtraction, efficiency normalization, and propagation of statistical uncertainties.
True visibility must be bounded with confidence intervals after accounting for accidental coincidences \(R_A R_B \tau_c\), dark counts, and postselection fractions.
A rigorous scientific conclusion explicitly states which alternative models the data rule out, which instrumental loopholes remain open, and how the analysis can be reproduced.
